scope: A local, proposed Google Business Profile photo set. No uploads, profile edits, pixel edits or website changes.

photo_review.method: Compare the two owner-selected replacement photos with the current Google Business Profile set. Check dominant subject, literal service labels and crop limits; preserve the reviewed source bytes.
photo_review.correction: Replace the smiling cover photo, ID 107, with the focused press-tool photo, ID 105. Replace the wider welding view, ID 23, with the closer grinding view, ID 20. Preserve both replaced JPEGs under superseded.
photo_review.selection_rule: Prefer candid work over posed eye contact. The customer's first visible subject must support the service label, and each replacement must add a distinct work process.
photo_review.crop_rule: These are unchanged full frames. Portrait equipment images need their vertical context; shallow landscape crops can remove vents, tanks, hands or fittings. Check Google's actual previews before publishing.

priority_source.user_priorities: Water heaters, dig jobs and leaks, drain stuff
priority_source.interpretation: Weight heater, underground pipe and plumbing work first. Keep hydronic heating and filtration visible as specialties. This is an editorial allocation, not a measured ranking of search demand, margins or conversions.

visual_system.palette: Natural copper, neutral walls, white fixtures and real equipment colors. Outdoor greens and soil remain unchanged.
visual_system.light: Readable equipment and faces; prefer sharp, evenly lit frames. Genuine utility-room light is acceptable when the subject remains clear.
visual_system.tone: Candid, documentary work and recognizable home fixtures. People focus on the task instead of posing or smiling at the camera.
visual_system.sequence: Start with focused tool use and the owner's priority work. Mix equipment, people and finished fixtures. Avoid near-identical views of the same equipment.
visual_system.treatment: Copy reviewed JPEG bytes without cropping, retouching, filters, color grading or AI changes. Show full frames in the review gallery.
visual_system.limits: Proposed numbers organize this package, not Google's public photo order. Google may choose another first or cover image. Photo count and filenames do not establish a ranking or website-traffic guarantee.

sources.title: Manage your services on your Business Profile
sources.use: Google permits suggested and custom services, grouping and descriptions; a matching service may be highlighted.

sources.title: Tips for business-specific photos
sources.use: Show representative work, specialty services and people. Images must represent reality.

sources.title: Manage your Business Profile photos and videos
sources.use: JPG/PNG, 10 KB to 5 MB, recommended 720 by 720 or larger, minimum 250 by 250. A selected cover need not appear first.

sources.title: Tips to improve your local ranking
sources.use: Local results depend mainly on relevance, distance and prominence. Complete business information matters; this source provides no uplift estimate for 15 photos.

photos.label: Technician using a press tool on copper heating pipework
photos.reason: Focused tool use and recognizable copper pipework introduce real work without a posed portrait.
photos.frame_note: Keep the face, hands, press tool and copper joint visible in Google's preview. Do not label the person by name without an identity record.

photos.label: Natural-gas tankless water heater and connections
photos.reason: A recognizable, sharp tankless heater shows a specific service customers can seek on the website.
photos.frame_note: Keep the vent and lower connections. Retain the equipment label; do not erase it.

photos.label: Electric storage water heater with expansion tank
photos.reason: The familiar tank complements the tankless photo and covers a different heater type without repeating one installation.
photos.frame_note: Use the full portrait frame. A shallow landscape crop loses the expansion tank or lower heater.

photos.role: Priority service: sewer and underground pipe work
photos.label: Replacement sewer branch connected in an open trench
photos.reason: The distinct pipe and replacement connection make underground sewer work understandable at a glance.
photos.frame_note: Keep the branch and existing pipe connection. This is open-trench work, not evidence of trenchless repair.

photos.label: Pressure-pipe route in an open yard trench
photos.reason: The long pipe route explains the scale of yard excavation and complements the sewer connection detail.
photos.frame_note: Keep the foreground blue pipe and the receding route. Do not call this trenchless work.

photos.label: Labeled hot and cold domestic-water distribution manifold
photos.reason: Orderly routing and readable shutoffs show plumbing detail without relying on an unverified repair story.
photos.frame_note: Keep upper copper feeds and the full manifold. This is domestic-water distribution, not a heating manifold.

photos.label: Crew beside removed clay sewer pipe and replacement sections
photos.reason: People and removed pipe show the work behind the cleaner connection photo and add residential yard context.
photos.frame_note: Keep the workers and removed clay pipe. Do not assign worker names or invent a before-and-after pairing.

photos.label: Worker connecting copper pipe beside a hot-water tank
photos.reason: A visible tank and active connection work add a human service view to the two heater photographs.
photos.frame_note: Keep the hands, tank and copper connection. The worker partly obscures the connections; use this as work in progress, not a finished-installation hero. The heat source is not established; do not label this gas, electric or heat-pump.

photos.label: Pedestal sink and three-piece faucet
photos.reason: A clean, familiar fixture connects technical work to the result a homeowner recognizes.
photos.frame_note: Keep the faucet and basin. Do not claim the image documents a leak repair.

photos.label: Bathtub with overhead and handheld shower fittings
photos.reason: The clear shower fittings show a different plumbing service from the sink, with the same calm residential finish.
photos.frame_note: The shower fittings sit on the left and the tub below. Preserve both in the full portrait frame; a centered square crop can leave too much bare tile and lose the showerhead. This is not paired with a construction photo as verified before-and-after.

photos.label: Water-supply and waste lines in an open wall
photos.reason: The wider wall view shows supply and drainage routing that a finished bathroom hides.
photos.frame_note: Keep red and blue supply runs and black waste branches. This is rough-in work, not drain cleaning or leak detection.

photos.label: Technician working on pipework beneath a wall-mounted heating appliance
photos.reason: The visible tool use and heating equipment show hands-on work within the hydronic specialty. This replaces an equipment-only circulation photograph.
photos.frame_note: Use the full portrait frame to keep the technician, tool, appliance and connected pipework visible. Shelves at left are part of the real setting. The photograph does not establish a specific repair, annual service or appliance subtype.

photos.role: People at work: checking pipe alignment
photos.label: Technician checking copper heating-pipe alignment with a level
photos.reason: The level, hands and copper pipe make the task clear. This adds a distinct work process while the sink and shower photos retain finished-home context.
photos.frame_note: Keep the level, both hands and copper pipe together in the full portrait frame. Preserve the work light and wall condition. This shows an alignment check, not proof of a completed repair or replacement.

photos.label: Water softener, UV chamber and cartridge filtration bank
photos.reason: A readable treatment layout shows the breadth of his water work and invites customers to understand the options on the site.
photos.frame_note: Keep the softener, separate brine tank, UV chamber and filter bank. Do not infer cartridge media from housing color.

photos.label: Worker grinding steel beside a pump assembly
photos.reason: The close view of the worker, sparks and pump assembly shows active field work with a stronger focal point than the wider frame.
photos.frame_note: Keep the worker, hands, grinder, sparks and pump assembly in the full portrait frame. The pump's served system is unverified; do not label it fire protection, domestic water, sump-pump or hydronic equipment. This shows grinding or cutting, not welding.

superseded_photos.reason: The sink and countertop dominate. The towel radiator remains a valid secondary object, but this frame is a poor heating-service lead. Retain its bytes for provenance; exclude it from the 15 upload candidates.
ID 80 retains hydronic heating coverage and adds a technician working on the pipework. Preserve this equipment overview outside the current 15-photo upload set.
ID 99 adds a clear pipe-alignment check. The sink and shower photos retain finished-home context; preserve this radiator view outside the current 15-photo upload set.
ID 23 adds welding action, while ID 28 retains a complete filtration overview. Preserve this second treatment setup outside the current 15-photo upload set.
ID 105 shows the same technician focused on the task instead of smiling at the camera. Preserve this earlier cover outside the upload set.
ID 20 provides a tighter, clearer view of active grinding and sparks. Preserve this wider work view outside the upload set.

cut_list.reason: Near-identical setting to the selected focused press-tool photo in ID 105. One clear introduction is enough.
A second tankless heater adds less variety than a storage tank and connection-work photograph.
More trench views add less than the selected connection, long pressure-pipe route and crew view.
Avoid filling the set with extra views of the same bathroom. Sink and shower already cover distinct subjects.
The clean overall plant is visibly softer at full size. The selected heating work photos add clearer human activity.
The sink and counter dominate a frame selected for its secondary towel radiator. The current heating picks show work on the heating pipework directly.
Replaced by the owner's work photos, IDs 80, 99 and 23. Preserve the earlier JPEGs under superseded; retain heater, excavation, sewer and filtration coverage in the current set.
Replaced at the owner's direction by focused action photos, IDs 105 and 20. Preserve the earlier JPEGs under superseded.
Additional industrial equipment views add less than the selected work processes and introduce harsher colors and flash.
The full treatment layout in ID 28 covers filtration; additional equipment details add less variety than the selected work photos.

coverage_gaps: No reviewed high-confidence photo shows leak detection, a burst-pipe repair or a leak-repair activity. Do not relabel a clean fixture or piping layout as that work.
No reviewed high-confidence photo shows drain-cleaning or hydrojetting action. Sewer replacement photographs cover a different service.
No reviewed photo establishes a trenchless method, a heat-pump water heater or radiant-floor pipework.
No real branded van photograph is available in this reviewed library. Simulated wrap mockups stay out of GBP.
No job city, work date, personal identity or before-and-after pairing is inferred from these images.
